title: Eighteen Years, Forty-Odd Stars, One Jungle. Welcome 3 Lands June 26 and It Wants the Whole Family Back in the Hall.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal and what feels like every comedian Bollywood ever loved reunite for Ahmed Khan's chaos. The 'Deewane Hain' video is pure 2007 nostalgia, weaponised.
body:
The song dropped and suddenly it was 2007 again. **Deewane Hain**, the new single from **Welcome to the Jungle**, opens on a frame so crowded with familiar faces it plays less like a music video and more like a class reunion you forgot you were invited to. Akshay Kumar, mid-step. Suniel Shetty, deadpan as ever. Raveena Tandon back in the frame after years. Paresh Rawal, Jacqueline Fernandez, Disha Patani, Arshad Warsi, Jackie Shroff — the camera barely lands on one before it has to make room for the next. A Kashmiri folk hook, *Rakshida Rakshida*, threads through it all, and by the second chorus you realise what the makers are actually selling: not a film, a feeling.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

That feeling has a release date now. **Welcome to the Jungle**, the long-gestating third chapter of the *Welcome* franchise, lands in cinemas worldwide on **26 June 2026** — six days out and counting.


> "Watch it on mute and it looks serious." — Director Ahmed Khan, on the film's unexpected straight face

Director **Ahmed Khan**, reuniting with Akshay after nineteen years, has been careful to manage expectations and stoke them at the same time. This is the comedy franchise built by the late **Neeraj Vora**, whose story credit anchors the film, with dialogue by Farhad Samji. Succeeding *Welcome* (2007) and *Welcome Back* (2015), it carries a tonne of goodwill and an even heavier cast. The premise is gloriously silly: a film crew heads into the forest to shoot a movie and walks straight into a different kind of danger. Khan shot it on a ten-acre jungle set at Film City in Goregaon, built a replica Kashmiri town alongside it, and then carted the whole circus to Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah for the romantic numbers.

Let's talk about that ensemble, because it is the entire pitch. Beyond the headliners, the call sheet reads like a roll-call of three decades of Hindi-film comfort food: **Lara Dutta**, Tusshar Kapoor, Shreyas Talpade, Aftab Shivdasani, Farida Jalal, Johnny Lever, Rajpal Yadav, Krushna Abhishek, Kiku Sharda, Daler Mehndi, Mukesh Tiwari, Urvashi Rautela — and a poignant final appearance from the late Pankaj Dheer. Sanjay Dutt reportedly joined the sets too. You don't assemble a cast this size for plot. You assemble it for the joy of watching people you grew up laughing at share one frame again.

Which is exactly the bet. Composer **Anand Raj Anand**, who wrote, sang and scored *Deewane Hain* alongside Amruta Fadnavis, said the quiet part out loud: he wasn't chasing trends. "I wanted to create something that feels familiar the moment you hear it," he noted — a wedding song, a festival song, a sing-it-together-at-3am song. In a year of grim mythological epics and brooding spy universes, *Welcome 3* is unapologetically the loud cousin who shows up to every party. The title track is a 2.0 of the original, with Shaan back on vocals. There is a song literally called *Ghis Ghis Ghis*. Subtlety was never invited.

For the diaspora, the timing is almost too neat. Akshay Kumar's franchises — *Housefull*, *Welcome*, the Rohit Shetty-adjacent chaos comedies — have always travelled, because they ask nothing of you except a Friday night and a willingness to laugh at the same joke your dad is laughing at one seat over. As a **Star Studio18** worldwide release, *Welcome to the Jungle* is built for exactly that overseas multiplex run — the AMC in Edison, the Cineworld in Wembley, the Cineplex in Brampton, all of which know precisely what to do with an Akshay Kumar summer entertainer.

The gamble, of course, is whether nostalgia alone can carry a film this stuffed. Ensemble comedies live and die by rhythm, and a cast this enormous can just as easily become noise. But Khan has been here before, and the *Deewane Hain* video suggests he knows precisely what he's making: a celebration, mounted at scale, that asks the audience to stop being clever for two hours and just have a good time.

Six days. Forty-something stars. One jungle. If it works, it'll be the kind of communal weekend the diaspora multiplex was built for. If it doesn't, well — at least the song is already stuck in your head.
